**Euclid** (; Ancient Greek: Εὐκλείδης; fl.300 BC) was an ancient Greek mathematician active as a geometer and logician.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBruno2003[httpsarchiveorgdetailsmathmathematicia00brunpage125_125]-2) Considered the "father of geometry",[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTESialaros2021%C2%A7_%22Summary%22-3) he is chiefly known for the _[Elements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid's\_Elements "Euclid's Elements")_ treatise, which established the foundations of geometry that largely dominated the field until the early 19th century. His system, now referred to as Euclidean geometry, involved innovations in combination with a synthesis of theories from earlier Greek mathematicians, including Eudoxus of Cnidus, Hippocrates of Chios, Thales and Theaetetus. With Archimedes and Apollonius of Perga, Euclid is generally considered among the greatest mathematicians of antiquity, and one of the most influential in the history of mathematics.

Very little is known of Euclid's life, and most information comes from the scholars Proclus and Pappus of Alexandria many centuries later. Medieval Islamic mathematicians invented a fanciful biography, and medieval Byzantine and early Renaissance scholars mistook him for the earlier philosopher Euclid of Megara. It is now generally accepted that he spent his career in Alexandria and lived around 300 BC, after Plato's students and before Archimedes. There is some speculation that Euclid studied at the Platonic Academy and later taught at the Musaeum; he is regarded as bridging the earlier Platonic tradition in Athens with the later tradition of Alexandria.
In the _Elements_, Euclid deduced the theorems from a small set of axioms. He also wrote works on perspective, conic sections, spherical geometry, number theory, and mathematical rigour. In addition to the _Elements_, Euclid wrote a central early text in the optics field, _[Optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid's\_Optics "Euclid's Optics")_, and lesser-known works including _[Data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid's\_Data "Euclid's Data")_ and _Phaenomena_. Euclid's authorship of _On Divisions of Figures_ and _Catoptrics_ has been questioned. He is thought to have written many lost works.

## Life
### Traditional narrative
[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:0_Chambre_de_Rapha%C3%ABl_-_%C3%89cole_d'Ath%C3%A8nes_-_Mus%C3%A9es_du_Vatican.JPG)
Detail of Raphael's impression of Euclid, teaching students in _The School of Athens_ (1509–1511)
The English name 'Euclid' is the anglicized version of the Ancient Greek name _Eukleídes_ (Εὐκλείδης).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTESialaros2021%C2%A7_%22Life%22-4)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-6) It is derived from 'eu-' (εὖ; 'well'), 'klês' (-κλῆς; 'fame'), meaning "renowned, glorious",[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTE''OED''b-7) and the suffix '-ides' (-ίδης, 'son of'). In English, by metonymy, 'Euclid' can mean his most well-known work, [Euclid's _Elements_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid's_Elements "Euclid's Elements"), or a copy thereof,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTE''OED''a-5) and is sometimes synonymous with 'geometry'.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBruno2003[httpsarchiveorgdetailsmathmathematicia00brunpage125_125]-2)

## Life
### Traditional narrative
As with many ancient Greek mathematicians, the details of Euclid's life are mostly unknown.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeath1981354-8) He is accepted as the author of four mostly extant treatises—the _Elements_, _[Optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid's\_Optics "Euclid's Optics")_, _[Data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid's\_Data "Euclid's Data")_, _[Phaenomena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid's\_Phaenomena "Euclid's Phaenomena")_—but besides this, there is nothing known for certain of him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAsper2010%C2%A7_para._1-9)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-11) The traditional narrative mainly follows the 5th century AD account by Proclus in his _Commentary on the First Book of Euclid's Elements_, as well as a few anecdotes from Pappus of Alexandria in the early 4th century.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTESialaros2021%C2%A7_%22Life%22-4)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-13)

## Life
### Traditional narrative
According to Proclus, Euclid lived shortly after several of Plato's (d.347 BC) followers and before the mathematician Archimedes (c.287– c.212 BC);[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-14) specifically, Proclus placed Euclid during the rule of Ptolemy I (r.305/304–282 BC).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeath1981354-8)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAsper2010%C2%A7_para._1-9)[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-15) Euclid's birthdate is unknown;

## Life
### Traditional narrative
some scholars estimate around 330[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBall1960[httpsarchiveorgdetailsshortaccountofhi0000ballpage52mode2up_52]-16)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTESialaros2020141-17) or 325 BC,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBruno2003[httpsarchiveorgdetailsmathmathematicia00brunpage125_125]-2)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoulding2010125-18) but others refrain from speculating.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmorynski20082-19) It is presumed that he was of Greek descent,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBall1960[httpsarchiveorgdetailsshortaccountofhi0000ballpage52mode2up_52]-16) but his birthplace is unknown.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyer1991[httpsarchiveorgdetailshistoryofmathema00boyepage100mode2upviewtheater_100]-20)[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-22) Proclus (a Neoplatonist) held that Euclid followed the Platonic tradition, but there is no definitive confirmation for this.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeath1981355-23) It is unlikely he was a contemporary of Plato,

## Life
### Traditional narrative
so it is often presumed that he was educated by Plato's disciples at the Platonic Academy in Athens.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoulding2010126-24) Historian Thomas Heath supported this theory, noting that most capable geometers lived in Athens, including many of those whose work Euclid built on;[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeath1908[httpsarchiveorgdetailsbub_gb_UhgPAAAAIAAJpagen13mode2up_2]-25) historian Michalis Sialaros considers this a mere conjecture.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTESialaros2021%C2%A7_%22Life%22-4)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTESialaros2020147%E2%80%93148-26) In any event, the contents of Euclid's work demonstrate familiarity with the Platonic geometry tradition.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBall1960[httpsarchiveorgdetailsshortaccountofhi0000ballpage52mode2up_52]-16)

## Life
### Traditional narrative
In his _Collection_, Pappus mentions that Apollonius studied with Euclid's students in Alexandria, and this has been taken to imply that Euclid worked and founded a mathematical tradition there.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAsper2010%C2%A7_para._1-9)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTESialaros2020142-27)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeath1908[httpsarchiveorgdetailsbub_gb_UhgPAAAAIAAJpagen13mode2up_2]-25) The city was founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BC,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBruno2003[httpsarchiveorgdetailsmathmathematicia00brunpage126_126]-28) and the rule of Ptolemy I from 306 BC onwards gave it a stability which was relatively unique amid the chaotic wars over dividing Alexander's empire.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBall1960[httpsarchiveorgdetailsshortaccountofhi0000ballpage50mode2up_51]-29) Ptolemy began a process of hellenization and commissioned numerous constructions, building the massive Musaeum institution,

## Life
### Traditional narrative
which was a leading center of education.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBoyer1991[httpsarchiveorgdetailshistoryofmathema00boyepage100mode2upviewtheater_100]-20)[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-31) Euclid is speculated to have been among the Musaeum's first scholars.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBruno2003[httpsarchiveorgdetailsmathmathematicia00brunpage126_126]-28) Euclid's date of death is unknown;
it has been speculated that he died c.270 BC.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBruno2003[httpsarchiveorgdetailsmathmathematicia00brunpage126_126]-28)

## Life
### Identity and historicity
Domenico Maroli's 1650s painting _Euclide di Megara si traveste da donna per recarsi ad Atene a seguire le lezioni di Socrate_ [_Euclid of Megara Dressing as a Woman to Hear Socrates Teach in Athens_]. At the time, Euclid the philosopher and Euclid the mathematician were wrongly considered the same person, so this painting includes mathematical objects on the table.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTESialaros2021%C2%A7_%22Life%22_and_Note_5-32)

## Legacy
The cover page of Oliver Byrne's 1847 colored edition of the _Elements_
Euclid is generally considered with Archimedes and Apollonius of Perga as among the greatest mathematicians of antiquity.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBall1960[httpsarchiveorgdetailsshortaccountofhi0000ballpage52mode2up_52]-16) Many commentators cite him as one of the most influential figures in the history of mathematics.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBruno2003[httpsarchiveorgdetailsmathmathematicia00brunpage125_125]-2) The geometrical system established by the _Elements_ long dominated the field; however, today that system is often referred to as 'Euclidean geometry' to distinguish it from other non-Euclidean geometries discovered in the early 19th century.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaisbakVan_der_Waerden2021%C2%A7_%22Legacy%22-78) Among Euclid's many namesakes are the European Space Agency's (ESA) Euclid space telescope,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-79) the lunar crater Euclides,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-80) and the minor planet 4354 Euclides.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-81)

## Legacy
The _Elements_ is often considered after the Bible as the most frequently translated, published, and studied book in the Western World's history.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaisbakVan_der_Waerden2021%C2%A7_%22Legacy%22-78) With Aristotle's _Metaphysics_, the _Elements_ is perhaps the most successful ancient Greek text, and was the dominant mathematical textbook in the Medieval Arab and Latin worlds.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaisbakVan_der_Waerden2021%C2%A7_%22Legacy%22-78)
The first English edition of the _Elements_ was published in 1570 by Henry Billingsley and John Dee.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoulding2010120-34) The mathematician Oliver Byrne published a well-known version of the _Elements_ in 1847 entitled _The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid in Which Coloured Diagrams and Symbols Are Used Instead of Letters for the Greater Ease of Learners_, which included colored diagrams intended to increase its pedagogical effect.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHawesKolpas2015-82)David Hilbert authored a [modern axiomatization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert's_axioms "Hilbert's axioms") of the _Elements_.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEH%C3%A4hlPeters2022%C2%A7_para._1-83)Edna St. Vincent Millay wrote that "Euclid alone has looked on Beauty bare."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-84)

As with many ancient Greek mathematicians, the details of Euclid's life are mostly unknown.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeath1981354-8) He is accepted as the author of four mostly extant treatises—the _Elements_, _[Optics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid's\_Optics "Euclid's Optics")_, _[Data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid's\_Data "Euclid's Data")_, _[Phaenomena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid's\_Phaenomena "Euclid's Phaenomena")_—but besides this, there is nothing known for certain of him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAsper2010%C2%A7_para._1-9)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-11) The traditional narrative mainly follows the 5th century AD account by Proclus in his _Commentary on the First Book of Euclid's Elements_, as well as a few anecdotes from Pappus of Alexandria in the early 4th century.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTESialaros2021%C2%A7_%22Life%22-4)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-13)

## Life
### Traditional narrative
In his _Collection_, Pappus mentions that Apollonius studied with Euclid's students in Alexandria, and this has been taken to imply that Euclid worked and founded a mathematical tradition there.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAsper2010%C2%A7_para._1-9)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTESialaros2020142-27)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeath1908[httpsarchiveorgdetailsbub_gb_UhgPAAAAIAAJpagen13mode2up_2]-25) The city was founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BC,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBruno2003[httpsarchiveorgdetailsmathmathematicia00brunpage126_126]-28) and the rule of Ptolemy I from 306 BC onwards gave it a stability which was relatively unique amid the chaotic wars over dividing Alexander's empire.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBall1960[httpsarchiveorgdetailsshortaccountofhi0000ballpage50mode2up_51]-29) Ptolemy began a process of hellenization and commissioned numerous constructions, building the massive Musaeum institution,

## Legacy
The cover page of Oliver Byrne's 1847 colored edition of the _Elements_
Euclid is generally considered with Archimedes and Apollonius of Perga as among the greatest mathematicians of antiquity.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBall1960[httpsarchiveorgdetailsshortaccountofhi0000ballpage52mode2up_52]-16) Many commentators cite him as one of the most influential figures in the history of mathematics.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBruno2003[httpsarchiveorgdetailsmathmathematicia00brunpage125_125]-2) The geometrical system established by the _Elements_ long dominated the field; however, today that system is often referred to as 'Euclidean geometry' to distinguish it from other non-Euclidean geometries discovered in the early 19th century.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaisbakVan_der_Waerden2021%C2%A7_%22Legacy%22-78) Among Euclid's many namesakes are the European Space Agency's (ESA) Euclid space telescope,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-79) the lunar crater Euclides,[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-80) and the minor planet 4354 Euclides.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-81)

## Legacy
The _Elements_ is often considered after the Bible as the most frequently translated, published, and studied book in the Western World's history.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaisbakVan_der_Waerden2021%C2%A7_%22Legacy%22-78) With Aristotle's _Metaphysics_, the _Elements_ is perhaps the most successful ancient Greek text, and was the dominant mathematical textbook in the Medieval Arab and Latin worlds.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTETaisbakVan_der_Waerden2021%C2%A7_%22Legacy%22-78)
The first English edition of the _Elements_ was published in 1570 by Henry Billingsley and John Dee.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGoulding2010120-34) The mathematician Oliver Byrne published a well-known version of the _Elements_ in 1847 entitled _The First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid in Which Coloured Diagrams and Symbols Are Used Instead of Letters for the Greater Ease of Learners_, which included colored diagrams intended to increase its pedagogical effect.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHawesKolpas2015-82)David Hilbert authored a [modern axiomatization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert's_axioms "Hilbert's axioms") of the _Elements_.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-FOOTNOTEH%C3%A4hlPeters2022%C2%A7_para._1-83)Edna St. Vincent Millay wrote that "Euclid alone has looked on Beauty bare."[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euclid#cite_note-84)
